name: ACS758LCB-050B-PFF-T
title: ACS758xCB family: Hall-effect linear current sensor with a 100 µΩ isolated primary conductor, ±50 A to ±200 A, 5-pin CB package
summary: A current sensor in which the measured current runs through a thick copper path inside the package (100 µΩ typ, terminals IP+ and IP–) and a chopper-stabilised Hall IC turns its magnetic field into an analog voltage on VIOUT, proportional to VCC. The primary is galvanically isolated from the three signal pins (4800 Vrms for 60 s). Variants cover ±50, ±100, ±150 and ±200 A bidirectional and 50 to 200 A unidirectional, in temperature grades L (–40 to 150 °C), K (–40 to 125 °C) and E (–40 to 85 °C), with three leadforms. ACS758LCB-050B-PFF-T is the ±50 A bidirectional L-grade part with 40 mV/A sensitivity and both terminals and signal pins formed. The family is marked not for new design (status change March 14, 2025); the named replacements are ACS772 and ACS773.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensor on a 3.3 V or 5 V supply with a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor from VCC to ground. The current to be measured, AC or DC, in one or both directions, passes through the primary path from IP+ to IP–. VIOUT reaches the output through series resistor RF, with CF from the output node to ground; CF is for noise, and its value depends on the application.

equations.name: Quiescent output, unidirectional
equations.note: Bidirectional parts sit at VCC / 2, 2.5 V at 5 V.

operation.text: The ACS758xCB remains in production, classed not for new design from March 14, 2025: it is sold only to existing applications, end of life is expected, and samples are no longer offered. ACS772 and ACS773 are the named substitutes.

Current through the copper path between IP+ (pin 4) and IP– (pin 5), 100 µΩ typ, sets up a magnetic field next to the die. A low-offset, chopper-stabilised BiCMOS Hall IC converts that field to a voltage on VIOUT. Gain and offset, and their temperature coefficients, are trimmed at the factory. The thick copper lets the part survive large overcurrents.

With no primary current a bidirectional part's output sits at VCC/2 (2.5 V at 5 V) and a unidirectional part's at 0.12 × VCC (0.6 V at 5 V). Current increasing from IP+ to IP– drives the output upward; on a bidirectional part that takes it above VCC/2. Trim resolution, magnetic hysteresis and thermal drift move the quiescent level; electrical offset VOE is its departure from VCC/2 (bidirectional) or 0.1 × VCC (unidirectional) from non-magnetic causes.

The primary terminals are electrically isolated from pins 1 to 3, so the part can sense on the high side of a high-voltage system without an optocoupler. A shield integrated in the package cuts capacitive coupling from the conductor to the die under fast dV/dt, keeping output ripple and offset drift low in high-side use.

Both the quiescent output and the sensitivity scale in proportion to VCC. Parts are trimmed at VCC = 5 V; running at another supply adds a little error from the nonlinearity of the ratiometric circuits. The supply range is 3.0 V to 5.5 V.
Sensitivity, in mV/A, is the product of the magnetic coupling (G/A) and the Hall amplifier gain (mV/G). The amplifier gain is set at the factory for best sensitivity at the half-scale current.
The noise floor comes from thermal and shot noise in the Hall element. Noise in mV divided by sensitivity in mV/A gives the smallest current the part can resolve.

Nonlinearity is how far the output departs from proportionality up to half-scale current; it arises as the flux concentrator starts to saturate near half-scale. Symmetry compares the output swing for positive and negative half-scale currents.

Remanent magnetism of the core material leaves a zero-current offset, largest after the magnetic circuit has been saturated by full-scale current or an overload, and larger at low temperatures. It depends mostly on the flux concentrator material.

Total output error ETOT is the greatest deviation of the output from its ideal value. It is considered in four regions: zero current at 25 °C, zero current over temperature, half-scale current at 25 °C and half-scale current over temperature.

Power-on time is how long the output takes, after VCC reaches its minimum operating level, to settle within ±10 % of its final value with a field applied. Rise time is the 10 % to 90 % interval of the output for a current step and sets the bandwidth, f(–3 dB) = 0.35 / tr. Eddy currents in a conductive IC ground plane lengthen both rise time and response time. Propagation delay comes from inductive loading in the IC package and in the loop formed by the primary conductor; it is a fixed time offset that can be compensated.

The Hall element's offset is separated from the field signal by modulation and demodulation: the DC offset is moved up in frequency and a low-pass filter removes it while the field signal passes. An anti-aliasing filter ahead of a sample-and-hold stops high-frequency signal components aliasing. The result is an offset that stays stable over temperature and mechanical stress and recovers precisely after thermal cycling.

RθJA is 7 °C/W on the Allegro evaluation board with 2800 mm² of 4 oz copper on the primary leadframe. One-second pulses at 1 % duty cycle of 1200 A at 25 °C, 900 A at 85 °C and 600 A at 150 °C are typical capabilities, bounded only by TJ(max) of 165 °C.

The part contains no lead (Pb); every lead is plated in 100 % matte tin. The thick leadframe is made from oxygen-free copper. The part is AEC-Q100 qualified, holds UL certified file US-29755-UL and TÜV America certificate U8V 15 05 54214 037, and is calibrated before shipment.
Uses named for the part: controlling motors and inverters, detecting and managing loads, regulating power supplies and DC-DC converters, and spotting overcurrent faults.

The PFF layout has two oblong slots for the formed current terminals (slot end radius 1.0 mm, arc centres 4 mm apart), each in a pad ringed by Ø0.5 mm through-holes, which are recommended. The three signal pins land on Ø0.8 mm holes with Ø1.5 mm pads at 1.91 mm pitch, 21.4 mm from the centre line of the current terminal slots.

The branded face carries the part number (NNNNNNN), temperature code and amperage range (TTT-AAA), lot number (LLLLLLL), year and week of manufacture (YYWW) and the supplier emblem; pin 1 is at the left. Scale and appearance of the branding vary by supplier.
